exposure: Hysteroscopic findings after adenomyomectomy (presence/absence/restoration of endometrial defects)
cohort: The study included 10 patients (11 pregnancies) who had undergone hysteroscopy following adenomyomectomy and later delivered at the study's hospital.
finding: The presence of an endometrial defect identified by postoperative hysteroscopy may be a risk factor for placenta accreta spectrum in subsequent pregnancies, but allowing sufficient recovery time for the endometrium may help reduce the risk of uterine rupture.
